title: Unspoken intermediates in the readout
takeaway: On three prompts whose answers depend on a concept that appears nowhere in the text — spider behind "the animal that spins webs", the planned rhyme fight, the English antonym big inside an all-Chinese task — the J-lens readout at middle layers names exactly that concept, before the final layers settle on the spoken answer. The figure establishes presence only; the causal test comes in Figure 13.
walkthrough:
This item is a live widget in the article, not a static image: three panels, each combining a prompt, one highlighted token position, and a short stack of layers, with the top [[j-lens-readout]] token printed beside each layer and a curved connector running from the stack to the position being read. Layer labels follow the paper's [[layer-percentage-indexing]] convention — 25 sampled layers relabeled 0 to 100 — so a label like L67 reads as a percentage of depth. The model is Claude Sonnet 4.5, the paper's default subject ([[claude-model-family]]). Unlike the article's opening lens widget, these panels are fixed: the prompt tokens are not clickable.

All three prompts share one design. The correct next token depends on an intermediate concept that the text never states, so anything the [[jacobian-lens]] shows of that concept was inferred, not copied in. This is the presence half of the section's case for [[internal-reasoning]]; the causal half follows in the next figure.

Panel 1, "Multihop Reasoning": the prompt "Fact: The number of legs on the animal that spins webs is", read at its final position. At L67 the top lens token is *spider*, with 0.98 of the readout mass in the widget's data. L83 splits between *legs*, *eight* and *spider*; L88 shows *eight*; L99 shows the output digit *8*. The word spider occurs in neither prompt nor answer, and it surfaces in the middle depths the paper identifies as [[workspace-layers]].

Panel 2, "Poetry Planning": the couplet opening "The soldier marched into the night," read at the line break, before any of the second line exists. At L54 the alternative rhyme *light* already sits at rank 3. At L75 the planned rhyme dominates, surfacing as *fighting* with *fight* also present. At L99, one position later, the lens gives *Prepared* — the word that in fact begins the second line. The rhyme is settled a full line before it can be spoken ([[rhyme-planning]]).

Panel 3, "Multilingual Antonyms": a prompt written entirely in Chinese, asking for the antonym of 小 ("small"). At L50 the top token is *Chinese* — the identity of the output language is itself a workspace item. At L62 and L75 the English tokens *bigger* and *big* carry the inferred antonym, consistent with the [[shared-multilingual-representation]] picture. Only at L99 does the readout become the Chinese answer 大.

Figure 13 then applies the [[lens-coordinate-swap]] to these same intermediates: exchanging spider for ant moves the output from "8" to "6".

terms.definition: The lens's read operation: at a chosen layer and token position, the residual-stream activation is projected through a corpus-averaged Jacobian and the unembedding, giving a softmax score for every vocabulary token. Each layer row in a panel prints the top-scoring token.

terms.term: L67, L83, L88, L99 (and the other L-labels)
terms.definition: Layer labels in the paper's percentage convention: 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers relabeled 0–100, so the number reads as a fraction of the model's depth. The final sampled layer (100) is displayed as L99 in this figure so it does not read as a layer count.
Title of the first panel: a two-hop factual prompt whose answer requires first inferring an unnamed bridging entity (spider) and then reporting one of its properties (eight legs).

Title of the second panel: completing a rhyming couplet requires choosing the second line's final rhyme word before writing the line, so the readout at the line break is checked for the planned rhyme.
Title of the third panel: an all-Chinese prompt whose intermediate computation shows up in English tokens, testing whether the model routes through an English-aligned shared representation.
The unspoken intermediate of panel 1: the animal that spins webs. It appears in the readout at L67 with 0.98 probability although the word is in neither the prompt nor the answer.

The answer taking shape across depth in panel 1: at L83 the readout splits between legs, eight and spider; by L88 the word eight dominates; at L99 it becomes the digit 8, the token the model actually emits.

The last word of the couplet's first line and the top readout token at L54 at the line break — the layer stack starts at content still tied to the just-read text, below the layer where the plan appears.

The planned rhyme of panel 2. At L75 the top token is fighting with fight also present; the panel caption names the plan fight, the word that ends the model's completion "Prepared to face the coming fight."
An alternative rhyme for "night", visible at rank 3 in the L54 readout. It is the swap target in Figure 13, where installing light in place of fight changes the completion to "morning light".
A rank annotation on a layer row: the named token is not the top of that readout but sits at the stated rank in the lens's token ranking.

The top readout token at L99 at the position after the line break — the model's actual next word, opening the second line. It shows the late layers holding the imminent output while the middle layers hold the plan.
Chinese for "small" and "big". The prompt asks for the antonym of 小; 大 is the correct answer and tops the readout only at L99, with 0.91 probability.
The bracketed gloss printed above panel 3's prompt: an English translation of the Chinese prompt, supplied by the figure, not part of what the model sees.
The top readout token at L50 in panel 3. The paper reads it as the model explicitly representing which language its output must be translated into, alongside thinking through the antonym in English.
English tokens carrying the inferred antonym in panel 3's middle layers: bigger tops the L62 readout at 0.93, big tops L75 at 0.58 with bigger at 0.36.
The curved line in each panel running from the layer stack to a highlighted prompt token: it marks the single token position at which every layer in that stack is being read.
The subject model, unnamed in the figure itself: the paper reports on Sonnet 4.5 by default and corroborates key results on Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5.

numbers.meaning: Panels, one per prompt: a two-hop fact (spider), a rhyming couplet (planned rhyme), and a Chinese antonym task (English-language intermediate). Section 3.3 adds a fourth, reward-driven example in Figure 14.

The paper reads the lens at 25 evenly spaced residual-stream layers and relabels them 0–100, so every L-number in the figure is a percentage of model depth, comparable across models of different layer counts.

The four layers shown in panel 1 (sampled-layer indices 16, 20, 21, 24). The readout moves from the inferred entity (spider at L67) through a mixed state (L83) to the answer word (eight, L88) and finally the emitted digit (8, L99) — intermediate first, answer last.
Probability of spider in the L67 readout of panel 1, from the widget's data files. Nearly all of that layer's lens mass is on a word absent from the text — the clearest single cell of the figure.
The L83 readout in panel 1: legs, eight, and spider in a near three-way split. The handoff layer where the inferred entity, the queried property, and the answer coexist.
Panel 1's late layers committing: eight holds 0.96 at L88, and the digit 8 holds 0.86 at L99. The same quantity changes surface form (word to digit) as depth approaches the output.
Panel 2's layers. L54 and L75 are read at the line break (the newline token); L99 is read one position later, where it shows Prepared, the model's actual next word.
Position of light in the L54 readout at the line break: an alternative rhyme already present but outranked. The top of that readout, night at 0.37, still echoes the line just read.
Probability of fighting at L75 at the line break (a capitalized variant adds 0.21) — the planned rhyme dominating the workspace a full line before it can be uttered.
Panel 3's layers, all read at the final quote mark of the Chinese prompt: language identity (Chinese) at L50, the English intermediate (bigger, big) at L62 and L75, and the Chinese answer 大 at L99.
Probability of Chinese atop the L50 readout in panel 3 — a low-confidence cell whose runners-up (language, opposite, word) describe the task rather than the answer.

Panel 3's main cells: bigger at L62 (0.93), big at L75 (0.58, with bigger at 0.36), and 大 at L99 (0.91). The antonym is computed in English at middle depth and translated to Chinese only near the output.

The section's causal follow-up, shown in Figure 13: swapping the spider lens vector for ant changes the model's top output from 8 to 6, the number of legs on an ant. This figure itself only establishes that spider is present.
